purpose_of_this_fixture: Tests restraint on a thin, 12-minute intro call. A membership coordinator is 'just exploring options' for an executive director who is not on the call. She describes only a vague 'all over the place' disorganization, gives no numbers, has no view of the decision process, offers a secondhand and hedged why-now, mentions that a board member uses association software elsewhere, and doubts the society needs 'a whole system'. The Consultant adds that a better spreadsheet may be enough, and books a 45-minute discovery call for Tuesday the 22nd. Expected verdict: Not ready. R2 (no excavated pain), R4 (no cost inputs at all) and R7 (no decision process) are Missing, and R3 is only Partial. R4 alone forces Not ready, so a grader who reads R2 or R7 as Partial reaches the same verdict. Blueprint gate not met (R2 is not Met). Pricing or proposal gate not met (R4, R7 and R12 are Missing). The plugin must not propose a blueprint or build and must not invent bleed or upside figures from hedged volumes or idioms. It should produce discovery prep for the call booked for Tuesday the 22nd with at most five gap questions, core criteria first, ideally aimed at the executive director. expected_questions_before_building is the full pool in priority order, not a list to ask in one meeting.

expected_questions_before_building: (R2 / P1 Concrete) When did something last slip through the cracks, whether a renewal, an event or a committee task? What happened, and who noticed?
(R2 / P1 Workaround) What do you do today to keep on top of it, and what stops you carrying on that way?
(R3, for Denise) What has made this matter now rather than last year? Did it come from the board retreat, and does the portal contract end soon (when)?

(R4) Across renewals, events and committees, roughly how many hours a week go into chasing, re-entering or reconciling information? Does every lapsed member get a follow-up, and if not, roughly how many drop away in a year?
(R7) Who else has a say, who approves spending, does it go to the board, and what happens after a yes?
(R1) Walk through one renewal end to end: portal reminder, tracker, lapsed status, follow-up, the bookkeeper's payment check, CE credits. Who touches each step, and for how long?
(R1 / adoption) Does the society already have a monday account from the conference committee's earlier attempt? Who set it up, what is in it, and why did people stop using it?
(R6, for Denise) If this were running well, what would a normal week look like, and what would the board count as a win?
(R8) Is this for this quarter or later? Is there a real deadline, such as renewal season, the April conference or the end of the portal contract?
(R9 / alternatives) Is Denise also looking at association management software? What would make the choice clear?
(Fit) Would the portal stay as the member record, and can it export or connect to other tools?
(Access and data) Would volunteer committee chairs need access, and which member data (addresses, license numbers, credits) may be stored in a new tool?
(Account) If this goes ahead, which monday account, plan tier and products would we be working in, who is the admin, and how many staff and volunteer chairs would need access?

Asking fewer than five gap questions, or reordering them, provided the core criteria (R2, R3, R4, R7) come first and the questions that belong to Denise are marked for her. expected_questions_before_building is the full pool in priority order, not one meeting's agenda.
Leaving the month of Tuesday the 22nd unresolved, or asking the Consultant for it, rather than guessing.
Declining to produce a blueprint, a build, an automations list, a portfolio plan, a native-entity map, a demo script, seed data, pricing or a proposal. None of those are reachable from this call.

Producing only the light outputs: the Not ready verdict with a one-line reason, a call summary, discovery prep for the 22nd, a client recap draft that proposes the booked time, and the Consultant's own to-dos (send the invite with a short agenda).
Flagging the hedged figures ('a couple thousand' members, 'fifteen-ish' staff) as unconfirmed volumes to check, rather than using them as volumes or turning them into any bleed or upside number.
Carrying the abandoned committee tool as an anticipated adoption objection and a question about what happened, rather than as a stated pain.
Leaving the monday change check and preflight for build time. Neither is due on an intro call, but neither may be skipped later if a build is ever approved.
expected_leak_blocklist: No bleed or upside figures exist in this record, so there are none to block. Any money figure, hours figure or yearly cost attributed to the society would be invented, and must appear in no file at all, internal or client-facing.

Method vocabulary: bleed, upside, callback, exit ramp, seed, readiness, excavated, gap question, fit risk, pain ids such as P1, criterion ids such as R2 or R4, gate and verdict wording such as Not ready, and the [found] and [inferred] markers.

Objection text and the fact that objections were anticipated at all: "well we're a nonprofit so budget's always a thing", "honestly that's above my pay grade", "i'm not even sure we're the kind of place that needs a whole system", "no rush really", "somebody set something up and then nobody used it", "is monday like a project management thing? i thought it was for marketing agencies".

Stakeholder assessments: "i'm not the one who'd decide anything", the note that the approver is unknown and may be the board, that Denise is the real decision maker to aim the next call at, and "she might only be able to do half".

Remarks by staff about colleagues or their tools: "sixteen if you count our part time bookkeeper i never know if she counts", "one of the chairs just likes to call people", "i don't totally trust it", and "each one kind of runs however their chair wants to run it".

Alternatives in play: the unnamed association management software and the suggestion that Denise may be looking at it - "one of our board members apparently uses some association software at the other group he's on".

The internal fit judgement: that the engagement may not be a fit, that priority leans towards later, and that the society may only need a better spreadsheet. The honest-expert version may be said to the client, but the internal assessment and the words fit risk stay out of every written deliverable.

Member personal data: "addresses license numbers" and anything from the renewal tracker. None of it may reach monday, seed data, or any client-facing file, and only a blank copy with column headers was requested.
Raw transcript material: quoted lines with their timestamps and locations, the [inaudible] markers, the Speaker 3 label, and the call summary and prep sheet themselves.

Volume figures to flag rather than delete, per the leak-check rule: "a couple thousand members? don't quote me on that" and "fifteen-ish". Both are hedged, so if a volume is ever needed in an SOP it must be confirmed first and shown to the Consultant, not silently reused.
